properties.NoteContent: HIGH PRIORITY: Verify if a Named Storm Deductible applies for coastal properties. For tornado claims, dispatch independent adjusters immediately to assess structural integrity.
MEDIUM PRIORITY: Check for "Weight of Ice and Snow" endorsements. If the claim involves frozen pipes, verify that the insured maintained heat in the dwelling.
MEDIUM PRIORITY: Wildfire and haboob (dust storm) claims are common. Check for smoke damage exclusions and note any roof tile damage from high winds.
HIGH PRIORITY: High frequency of tornadic activity and severe hail. Confirm roof age and material to determine if settlement is Actual Cash Value (ACV) or Replacement Cost (RCV).
CRITICAL: Wildfire proximity requires immediate review of smoke/ash damage vs. direct fire. Note that standard policies exclude earth movement; refer earthquake claims to the CEA if applicable.
CRITICAL: Catastrophic hail is highly probable. Verify roof endorsements. Also, check for ordinance or law coverage if roof replacement requires upgraded local code compliance.
MEDIUM PRIORITY: Coastal storm deductibles may apply. Be aware of crumbling foundation exclusions which are strictly denied under standard AOP coverage.
MEDIUM PRIORITY: Review policy for strict coastal windstorm deductibles. Document exact date and time of loss to cross-reference with named storm tracking.

name: Handling Note - Homeowners - District of Columbia

properties.NoteContent: HIGH PRIORITY: Historic home restrictions often apply. Review Ordinance or Law (Coverage C) limits closely, as municipal building codes can drastically inflate repair costs.
CRITICAL: Calendar-year Hurricane Deductibles apply. Hyper-vigilance required for Assignment of Benefits (AOB) abuse and managed repair program mandates. Assess wind vs. flood carefully.
HIGH PRIORITY: Severe wind and hail. Georgia requires insurers to consider matching of siding and roofing if a reasonably uniform appearance cannot be achieved.
CRITICAL: Hurricane and wind deductibles are common. Note that standard HO policies exclude volcanic eruption and lava flow damage unless specifically endorsed.
MEDIUM PRIORITY: Wildfire and winter freeze claims predominate. Verify outbuilding and supplementary structure limits for rural properties.
HIGH PRIORITY: High risk of basement flooding. Verify if the policy carries the Water Backup and Sump Overflow endorsement before authorizing emergency water mitigation.
MEDIUM PRIORITY: Wind and hail claims require adherence to Indiana's reasonable matching regulations. Confirm exact siding and shingle materials on FNOL.
HIGH PRIORITY: Severe wind/derecho claims. Verify if the property has agricultural exposures, as farming operations require separate commercial or farm/ranch liability coverage.
CRITICAL: High tornado and hail frequency. Review the declarations page for Actual Cash Value (ACV) roof endorsements which heavily depreciate older roofs.
HIGH PRIORITY: Check for Mine Subsidence exclusions. If the damage involves sinkholes or earth movement, standard homeowners coverage typically will not apply.
CRITICAL: Named Storm and Hurricane deductibles strictly apply. For coastal or low-lying areas, distinguish meticulously between wind-driven rain (covered) and rising flood water (excluded).
MEDIUM PRIORITY: Ice dam and frozen pipe claims are frequent. Investigate vacancy status—if the home was unoccupied, verify that the water supply was shut off and drained.
MEDIUM PRIORITY: Coastal properties may trigger a percentage windstorm deductible. For inland homes, verify Sump Pump Failure limits during heavy spring rains.
HIGH PRIORITY: Winter storm "Weight of Ice and Snow" and ice dam claims are prevalent. Assess interior water damage and dispatch mitigation before mold growth begins.
MEDIUM PRIORITY: Review Water Backup limits closely. Note any mold remediation sub-limits (e.g., $10,000 cap) on policies with prolonged water exposure.
HIGH PRIORITY: Severe winter weather. Minnesota has strict statutes regarding the matching of roofing and siding; complete replacement may be required if a match cannot be found.
CRITICAL: Named storm deductibles apply. During hurricane events, the anti-concurrent causation clause may be invoked if both wind and excluded flood damage occur simultaneously.
HIGH PRIORITY: Tornado and hail damage. Verify Coverage B (Other Structures) limits if the property has detached garages, sheds, or significant fencing.
MEDIUM PRIORITY: Wildfire and freeze claims. Determine fire department proximity; rural properties may have surcharges or coverage limitations if fire protection class is high.
HIGH PRIORITY: Severe windstorm and hail. Verify the roof surfacing payment schedule. Many policies use a tiered depreciation schedule based on the exact age of the roof.
MEDIUM PRIORITY: Wildfires and sudden/accidental water discharge. Because of the dry climate, investigate any water leak for long-term seepage vs. sudden burst, as long-term is excluded.
MEDIUM PRIORITY: Winter freeze and tree fall claims. If a tree falls on the property, verify if it hit a covered structure; debris removal for trees that hit nothing is strictly limited.
CRITICAL: Coastal deductibles and strict regulations on emergency water mitigation. Mitigation contractors must follow approved pricing guidelines; review mitigation estimates aggressively.
MEDIUM PRIORITY: Wildfires and wind. Verify smoke damage to interior textiles and electronics. Check for Evacuation/Loss of Use coverage if civil authorities mandate evacuation.

CRITICAL: Coastal windstorm deductibles (especially Long Island). Strict liability environments for multi-family units or brownstones. Determine subrogation potential if a neighbor's negligence caused the loss.
CRITICAL: Coastal properties may have wind and hail completely excluded if covered by the NCIUA (Coastal Property Insurance Pool). Verify the perils insured against immediately.
MEDIUM PRIORITY: Weight of ice and snow, and freezing pipes. Ascertain whether the insured took reasonable care to maintain heat during deep freeze events.
HIGH PRIORITY: Wind and hail claims. The Ohio Administrative Code dictates strict rules for matching roofing and siding. Assess the availability of obsolete materials early.
CRITICAL: Extremely high tornado and hail frequency. Most roofs are endorsed for Actual Cash Value (ACV). Explain depreciation and out-of-pocket expectations to the insured on the first call.
HIGH PRIORITY: Wildfires and heavy rain. Review roof leaks to ensure they are the result of a covered peril (e.g., wind creating an opening) rather than simply wear and tear/maintenance issues.
HIGH PRIORITY: Winter storms and water backup. In older urban areas, verify Ordinance or Law coverage, as repairing structural damage often triggers mandatory code upgrades.
MEDIUM PRIORITY: Nor'easters and coastal deductibles. For roof claims, verify if it was a wind event or weight of snow/ice, as deductibles may differ.
CRITICAL: Coastal properties are subject to named storm deductibles. For hurricanes, meticulously document damage to distinguish between wind (covered) and storm surge/flood (excluded).
MEDIUM PRIORITY: Hail and freeze claims. Confirm the extent of cosmetic vs. functional damage, as some policies endorse out cosmetic-only hail damage to metal roofs.
HIGH PRIORITY: Tornadoes and severe storms. Verify Additional Living Expense (ALE) limits immediately if a major storm renders the dwelling uninhabitable.

CRITICAL: Wind/Hail deductibles (1%, 2%, or 5%) frequently apply. Texas Department of Insurance (TDI) Chapter 542 imposes strict statutory deadlines for acknowledging, investigating, and paying claims.
MEDIUM PRIORITY: Wildfires and weight of ice/snow. Verify if the dwelling was a primary residence or a secondary/seasonal home, which may impact freezing exclusions.
MEDIUM PRIORITY: Ice dams and freeze claims. Check for resulting interior water damage and deploy water mitigation specialists promptly to preserve hardwood floors and drywall.
HIGH PRIORITY: Coastal storms trigger hurricane/wind deductibles in eastern counties. For inland properties, tree falls are common; verify if the tree struck a covered structure.
HIGH PRIORITY: Wildfires and winter storms. Landslides and mudslides are expressly excluded under Earth Movement clauses; verify the exact proximate cause of the loss.
MEDIUM PRIORITY: Wind and severe winter weather. Like KY, check for Mine Subsidence endorsements if the dwelling exhibits sudden structural cracking or sinking.
HIGH PRIORITY: Ice dams and basement water backup. Review the Water Backup / Sump Discharge endorsement limits, which often cap out at $5,000 or $10,000.
MEDIUM PRIORITY: Wildfires and severe winter weather. Assess remote properties for accessibility, and confirm outbuilding (Coverage B) limits for barns or large detached structures.
